latest_apis.rationale: Everything here is the current generation: latest stable Vite 8 (Rolldown/Oxc era) and TypeScript 7, using only the current config and client APIs. The only quibble is the hard-coded `chrome120` target (Dec 2023 browser) where Vite 8's default or 'esnext' would need even less transpilation — a choice, not a legacy pattern.

platform.rationale: Good modern-platform instincts (fetch, URL/URLSearchParams, history API, lazy images, custom properties, streaming file server), but the two places where the platform offers a clearly better tool are missed: no AbortController for cancellable navigation loads, and DOM built from raw strings with a hand-rolled escaper plus an inline event-handler attribute.

evidence: app/package.json:12-14 — exactly two devDependencies, zero runtime dependencies
app/server.mjs:1-4 — 90-line static server on node:http instead of pulling express or a static-file package
app/src/main.ts:74-93 — hand-rolled 20-line history-API router instead of a routing library

dependencies.rationale: Minimal and modern: the platform covers routing, serving and styling, so nothing was added. Both devDeps are the current stable majors. The only blemish is that TypeScript is installed but never executed (see churn_resistance), so it currently earns its keep only in the editor.

evidence: app/src/api.ts:152-390 — all network access, caching and record types behind one module; pages never call fetch directly except via apiFetch
app/src/main.ts:40-62 — routing is one flat dispatch; adding a page touches one file
app/src/pages/home.ts:16-23 — single buildUrl() owns query-state shape; components.ts:9-23 owns href shapes
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:144 — apiFetch<any>(url) and :150 record: any punch through the typed boundary
app/package.json:6-10 — build script is only 'vite build'; no 'tsc --noEmit' step despite tsconfig.json:15 noEmit, so type errors never fail the build
app/src/components.ts:6-15 — escapeHtml must be remembered at ~40 interpolation sites; some values are deliberately interpolated raw (app/src/pages/details.ts:38-40)
app/src/api.ts:1-5 — window.__API_BASE_URL__ read through an inline cast rather than an ambient declaration in vite-env.d.ts
churn_resistance.rationale: The architecture is genuinely churn-resistant — data, routing and URL construction each live in exactly one place with types at the boundary. What will bite later: the hand-rolled string-templating convention depends on per-interpolation escaping discipline, and with no typecheck in the build the otherwise good types can silently rot. Fixing the two `any`s and adding a typecheck script would make this a 5.

findings.issue: `build` runs only `vite build`; Vite never type-checks, so TypeScript 7 is installed but `tsc --noEmit` never runs and type errors cannot fail a build.
findings.suggestion: Add `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"` and run it as part of `build` (or at least in CI).

findings.issue: `apiFetch<any>(url)` and `record: any` (line 150) bypass the typed API boundary, and unlike every other record the move data used to build rows is untyped.
findings.suggestion: Type it as `MoveRecord` (the interface already exists in app/src/api.ts:105) and reuse `englishName`/`humanize` helpers.

findings.issue: Rendering is raw string concatenation into `innerHTML` with a hand-maintained `escapeHtml` at ~40 interpolation points across pages; one missed escape is an XSS bug, and raw interpolation is already mixed with escaped values (app/src/pages/details.ts:38-40).
findings.suggestion: Centralize safety with a small tagged-template helper that escapes interpolated values by default, or build DOM via `<template>` + `textContent` for the data-bearing parts.

findings.issue: No `AbortController` on fetches; navigating away abandons loads that still run to completion, and the render guard is a hand-rolled token counter duplicated per page (`renderToken` in app/src/main.ts:29, `gameRequest` in app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:380).
findings.suggestion: Pass an `AbortSignal` per route render, or hoist the request/token guard into api.ts so the pattern isn't re-implemented.

findings.issue: Inline `onerror` attribute on the card sprite; inline handlers are the first thing a strict CSP breaks and are invisible to TS.
findings.suggestion: Attach an `error` listener when the card list is inserted, or use CSS (empty-src styling) / a placeholder image.

findings.issue: `build.target: 'chrome120'` pins transpilation to a Dec-2023 browser; Vite 8's default `'baseline-widely-available'` or `'esnext'` (spec says latest Chromium only) would need less transpilation and one less thing to bump.
findings.suggestion: Drop the override or use `'esnext'` given the Chromium-only requirement.

findings.issue: Runtime config read via `(window as unknown as { __API_BASE_URL__?: string }).__API_BASE_URL__` cast.
findings.suggestion: Declare the global ambient type in app/src/vite-env.d.ts so the config boundary is typed like everything else.

findings.issue: `renderIndex` re-reads `dist/index.html` synchronously with `fs.readFileSync` on every request, blocking the event loop per hit.
findings.suggestion: Read once at startup (invalidate on change) and use `fs/promises`, matching the streaming path used for other assets.

findings.issue: `target: ES2022` with TS 7 available; harmless, but a 2022 language floor is older than it needs to be.
findings.suggestion: Consider ES2023/ESNext now that the build target is a modern browser.

summary: This is a lean, current stack: Vite 8.3.5 and TypeScript 7.0.2 (both the latest stable majors as of October 2026), zero runtime dependencies, and a self-contained data layer in api.ts that keeps routing, URL shaping and fetching each in one place. The forward-looking gaps are in the layer Vite can't help with: hand-rolled innerHTML templating whose safety rests on remembering escapeHtml at every interpolation, no AbortController for abandoned route loads, two `any`s at the otherwise-typed boundary, and a build script that never runs `tsc`. Cheap fixes; the architecture underneath them will age well.

apis.replacement: Pass an AbortSignal per route render to cancel superseded loads
